notes: Flat rate: 'The state income tax rate for 2025 is 3.07 percent (0.0307)' (PDF page 1); PA-40 line 12: 'Multiply Line 11 by 3.07 percent (0.0307)'. One rate for every filing status. The form prints Single, Married Filing Jointly and Married Filing Separately; the booklet has no head of household status, and a surviving spouse filing separately uses Single (PDF page 8). No separate schedule is printed, so only single and married_joint lists are given.

Standard deduction and exemptions: the booklet says there are none: 'PA law does not allow standard deductions, deductions for personal exemptions, itemized deductions, or deductions for personal expenses' (PDF page 9). No age-65 or blindness amount is printed. Only Line 10 Other Deductions exist.

Line 10 Other Deductions (PDF page 20): student loan interest up to 2,500 and Section 529 contributions up to 19,000 per beneficiary per taxpayer are recorded. Medical Savings Account and Health Savings Account contributions follow federal rules and limits and ABLE contributions are deductible (PDF pages 9, 20); no amount is printed for these three. The page says 'five deductions', names four in its sentence and lists six codes (M, H, S, T, A, C), one of them 'Combined'. Schedule O is not among the sources.

Base: PA has no federal starting point. Line 9 adds 'only the positive income amounts' from Lines 1c, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 (form; PDF page 20), and 'You cannot use a loss that you report in one income class on your tax return to reduce income in any other class' (PDF page 20). 'Federal income classifications are disregarded to the extent they are inconsistent with PA classifications' (PDF page 8). Spouses cannot offset each other's income and losses, even on a joint return (PDF page 15), and gains and losses do not carry to other years (PDF page 15).

Social Security and Railroad Retirement: 'INCOME NOT TAXABLE FOR PA PIT PURPOSES' lists 'Social Security benefits and/or Railroad Retirement benefits' (PDF page 8). Second source: Guide, Gross Compensation: 'Retirement income, such as: distributions from eligible Pennsylvania retirement plans* after retirement age; Social Security payments; railroad retirement benefits'. The PA-40 has no Social Security line (form). Social Security is held in social_security.treatment only.

Pensions from other states' governments, New York State's included: no source names one; 'New York' is printed in none of the three documents. Settled as a reading, in the covers of employer_plan_after_retirement, because the rule is written by kind of plan, not by payer: 'Pennsylvania does not impose income tax on payments you receive that are commonly recognized retirement benefits distributed from eligible employer-sponsored retirement plans' (PDF page 11); 'Commonly recognized pension, old age, or retirement benefits paid after becoming eligible to retire, and retiring' are not taxable (PDF page 8); and the eligibility test is four characteristics of the plan, none about the employer or place (PDF page 13 Filing Tip 2; Guide, 'Criteria for A Plan to Qualify as an Eligible Pennsylvania Retirement Plan'). The Guide's name 'eligible Pennsylvania retirement plan' means eligible for PA tax, as the same Guide's 'eligible plan for PA PIT purposes' shows; it is not a plan run by Pennsylvania. Another state's pension is not in the named list on PDF page 12 item 5, so it needs the plan test and retirement, unlike the named systems, and is not in public_pension_pa_federal_plans. A private plan stands in the same position: exempt only if the plan passes.

No paying_states: the reciprocal agreements with Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, Ohio, Virginia and West Virginia cover compensation (PDF page 11), and 'These agreements apply to employee compensation only' (Guide). New York is not one of them. When such a distribution is taxable, the Guide says 'Residents who contributed to a retirement plan while a nonresident are subject to tax only on the amount received over and above their contributions, regardless of whether tax was paid to another state on the retirement income.'

The four systems named on PDF page 12 item 5, in the booklet's words: 'the State Employees' Retirement System, the Pennsylvania School Employees' Retirement System, the Pennsylvania Municipal Employees' Retirement System, and the U.S. Civil Service Commission Retirement Disability Plan'. The entry's label shortens the last name so the cross-state report does not file the entry as a narrow disability case; it is the general rule for those systems.

Pennsylvania local and county government plans other than the Pennsylvania Municipal Employees' Retirement System are not named; they fall under the plan test, so public_pension is also in the covers of employer_plan_after_retirement.

IRA, booklet against Guide: the booklet says 'Distributions you receive after retiring but before age 59 1/2 are taxable even if you receive substantially equal payments, and you do not pay the federal penalty for an early withdrawal. PA law does not have any exceptions similar to the federal exceptions for withdrawal before age 59 1/2' (PDF page 12). The Guide says the department treats an IRA distribution as exempt 'so long as the taxpayer is not required to pay a penalty for early withdrawal', giving 'retirement, death, disability, separation from service unforeseeable emergency or attaining the age of 59 1/2'. They disagree for a penalty-free withdrawal before 59 1/2 by someone neither dead nor disabled. The 2025 booklet is the year's own document and is the more specific, so min_age 59.5 stands; the disability case has its own entry from PDF page 13.

Roth conversions: exempt when the entire withdrawal goes trustee to trustee, or 'within 60 days invested the entire (100 percent) amount you received into a Roth IRA' (PDF page 12), with any federal tax withheld also put in (PDF page 12 CAUTION; PDF page 13 Filing Tip 4). What is not rolled over is taxable to the extent it exceeds the adjusted basis (Filing Tip 4). 'Entire' means the whole withdrawal, not the whole IRA. On or after 59 1/2 the part kept is still an IRA distribution exempt under ira_distribution_age_59_5. The rule printed is traditional IRA to Roth IRA only. A rollover from an employer plan counts as exempt under PDF page 12 item 2 'only when the transferred amounts are not taxable income for federal purposes', so a Roth rollover from a 401(k) rests on item 1 (qualified and retired).

Annuities: a commercial insurance or mutual company annuity, an annuity outside an employer-sponsored program, an endowment contract and a charitable gift annuity are interest income to the extent federally reported (PDF pages 13, 15), so they have no relief. An annuity from an eligible employer plan after retirement is employer_plan_annuity (PDF page 13 Box 8).

Municipal interest: taxable interest includes 'obligations of other states (not Pennsylvania)' (PDF page 14) and 'Obligations of other states or countries' (PDF page 31); direct obligations of the Commonwealth and its political subdivisions are not taxable (PDF pages 14, 31; Schedule A line 6).

Capital gains: 'PA law does not distinguish between long-term and short term gains (losses)' (PDF page 17) and no rate or deduction differs. Mutual fund capital gains distributions are dividends on Line 3 (PDF pages 15, 18), at the same rate.

Tax Forgiveness (PA Schedule SP, PA-40 lines 19a to 21; PDF pages 36-39) is recorded as tax_forgiveness with income_test.effect stepped. The fields hold the no-dependent columns of Tables 1 and 2. Each dependent child adds 9,500 to every column (6,500 becomes 16,000; the tables print nine children), which no step field holds; it is in who.other_conditions. Eligibility Income has no equivalent in the schema's measures: it is Line 9 PA taxable income plus listed nontaxable income, and it leaves out Social Security, Railroad Retirement, eligible retirement benefits, military pensions and Civil Service annuities (PDF pages 38-39).

Other credits are not recorded: Resident Credit for tax paid to other states (Line 22, PA Schedule G-L, not in the booklet), PA Schedule OC restricted credits, and the Schedule DC child and dependent care credit (Line 23; PDF pages 22-23).
Surtaxes and recapture: none printed. Inflation: the booklet and the Guide say nothing of adjusting the rate or any other figure; not found in the sources.
